# gpupaas_kubernetes_cluster_status (Data Source)

The live status of a managed Kubernetes cluster: its lifecycle, health, the upgrade targets and, for the control plane and each worker pool, the nodes the platform reports with their addresses and Kubernetes conditions. Unlike `gpupaas_kubernetes_cluster` it reads the platform's status document, which joins the declared pools with what runs behind them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gpupaas_kubernetes_cluster_status" "c" {
  project = "system-catalog"
  cluster = "my-cluster"
}

output "cluster_health" {
  value = data.gpupaas_kubernetes_cluster_status.c.health
}

# The private IP of every control-plane node.
output "control_plane_ips" {
  value = [for n in data.gpupaas_kubernetes_cluster_status.c.control_plane.nodes : n.private_ip]
}

# The nodes that are not ready, per worker pool.
output "unready_nodes" {
  value = {
    for p in data.gpupaas_kubernetes_cluster_status.c.worker_pools :
    p.name => [for n in p.nodes : n.hostname if n.state["ClusterNodeReady"] != "true"]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `cluster` (String) Name of the cluster.
- `project` (String)

### Read-Only

- `action` (String)
- `available_kubernetes_versions` (List of String) Versions the cluster can be upgraded to.
- `control_plane` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--control_plane))
- `health` (String) Overall health: `healthy`, `unhealthy`, `degraded` or `unknown`.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `kubernetes_version` (String)
- `location` (String)
- `phase` (String) Normalized status: `provisioning`, `running`, `updating`, `upgrading`, `degraded`, `error`, `destroying`, ...
- `reason` (String)
- `status` (String) Raw status, for example `MKS_CLUSTER_STATUS_RUNNING`.
- `worker_pools` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--worker_pools))

<a id="nestedatt--control_plane"></a>
### Nested Schema for `control_plane`

Read-Only:

- `compute_type` (String)
- `datacenter` (String)
- `health` (String) Health of the pool: `healthy`, `unhealthy`, `degraded` or `unknown`.
- `name` (String) Empty for the control plane.
- `nodes` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--control_plane--nodes))
- `os_image` (String)
- `platform` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--control_plane--platform))
- `sku_name` (String)
- `sku_type` (String)
- `status` (String) The pool's lifecycle: `CREATING`, `ACTIVE`, `UPDATING`, `DELETING`, `CREATE_FAILED` or `DELETE_FAILED`. It is not machine health.

<a id="nestedatt--control_plane--nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `control_plane.nodes`

Read-Only:

- `arch` (String)
- `hostname` (String)
- `kubernetes_version` (String)
- `labels` (Map of String)
- `os` (String)
- `private_ip` (String)
- `roles` (List of String) `Master` and/or `Worker`.
- `state` (Map of String) Kubernetes conditions (`DiskPressure`, `MemoryPressure`, `PIDPressure`, `NetworkUnavailable`, `ClusterNodeReady`) as `true`, `false` or `unknown`.
- `status` (String) The platform's own status word for the node, for example `READY`.


<a id="nestedatt--control_plane--platform"></a>
### Nested Schema for `control_plane.platform`

Read-Only:

- `components` (Map of String) Installed component versions by display name.
- `version` (String) The platform build the pool's nodes run.
